title: AI Pipe
summary: A self-hostable LLM API gateway that simplifies access to language models, particularly for front-end applications.
overview: AI Pipe lets web apps call LLM APIs (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Gemini) without a back end. A hosted instance runs at aipipe.org, and the MIT-licensed code can be self-hosted on Cloudflare.
capabilities: OpenAI-compatible endpoints: set a base URL and an AI Pipe token in any OpenAI-style client or CLI.
Google sign-in issues a personal token and shows usage, so apps do not need to ship provider keys.
Native provider keys (OpenAI/OpenRouter `sk-`, Gemini `AIza`) can be passed straight through instead of a token.
A small JavaScript helper (`aipipe.js`) handles the login redirect for pure front-end apps.
A playground page for exploring models and chatting with them.
useCases: Prototyping browser-only LLM apps without a server.
Giving workshop or classroom participants model access without sharing provider keys.
Running a team-owned gateway on Cloudflare.

title: LLM Pricing and Quality Explorer
summary: Compare language models by cost and quality, identify cost-performance frontier models, and explore how the frontier changes over time.
overview: An interactive chart that plots each LLM's representative API input price per million tokens against its Arena Elo score, and marks which models are Pareto-optimal (nothing is both cheaper and better).
capabilities: Cost-versus-quality scatter plot with Pareto-optimal models highlighted green and dominated models red.
A month slider that shows how model economics compare across model lifetimes, with one representative price per model.
Data kept in `elo.csv`, refreshed from the Arena leaderboards by Python scripts that have offline tests.
Documented pricing rules: prefer durable first-party or mainstream-provider prices over promotional routes.
useCases: Shortlisting models for a given budget and quality bar.
Tracking how the cost-quality frontier moves as new models launch.

title: Tools in Data Science
summary: Learning materials for IIT Madras's Tools in Data Science course, covering practical data science and software engineering workflows.
overview: The course content for Tools in Data Science, a diploma-level course at IIT Madras. The repository holds one folder per term, shared topic pages and live-session summaries, and builds a static site with Hugo.
capabilities: Term-by-term content folders (Jan 2025 through Sep 2026) with a current-term home page.
Shared topic pages published at the site root, such as Bash.
FAQ-style summaries of recorded live sessions.
A Hugo build with a draft flag so unreleased weeks can stay hidden until published.
Prompts used to generate or review the content are kept alongside it.
useCases: Students following the course term by term.
Instructors adapting the structure or topic pages for similar courses.

title: AI-Powered Web Tools
summary: A collection of lightweight web utilities, many developed using language models, for practical everyday tasks.
overview: A set of single-page web apps and bookmarklets, mostly written with LLMs, hosted at tools.s-anand.net. Each tool does one small job in the browser.
capabilities: Bookmarklets that copy AI conversations, Hacker News threads, Discourse topics or web pages as Markdown or JSON.
Converters and helpers such as JSON to CSV and a Markdown-to-Unicode formatter.
Google Tasks export to CSV or Markdown, and GitHub helpers (stars, summaries, user info).
AI-assisted generators, including podcast, image and poster generators.
A local music player and recording tools that work offline in the browser.
useCases: Capturing web and chat content as Markdown for notes and knowledge bases.
Quick data wrangling without installing software.

title: Interactive Data Stories
summary: A collection of data visualizations and interactive stories that communicate insights through visual exploration.
overview: Small, mostly vibe-coded data stories, each a self-contained page with its own dataset and narrative, published as a site with a screenshot per story.
capabilities: Explorable atlases, for example tall buildings (height versus floor count) and embassies sent abroad versus GDP.
Forecast and reliability analyses, such as IMF GDP forecast errors and Wikipedia citation fragility.
Narrative pieces that pair a data story with interactive charts.
A `config.json` and Just recipes drive the site build.
useCases: Reference examples for data storytelling and chart design.
Starting points for new interactive data pieces.

links.label: Screenshot: AI agents for science story

title: Business LLM Demonstrations
summary: A collection of language-model demonstrations illustrating practical business applications and opportunities for AI adoption.
overview: A catalogue of mostly LLM demos with business use cases. The README is explicit that these are personal, MIT-licensed open-source projects, not official products of any employer, and contain no confidential data or IP.
capabilities: Demos are listed in a `config.json` and built into a static catalogue page with `just build`.
Adding a demo means adding an entry and committing; the repository includes tests and a helper-workflow guide (`AGENTS.md`).
Open-source (MIT) so demos can be studied and reused.
useCases: Browsing concrete examples when discussing where LLMs could help a business process.
Seeding ideas for internal AI prototypes.

links.label: Talk: Intro to Large Language Models (Andrej Karpathy)

title: Reusable Agent Skills
summary: Reusable instructions and workflows for AI agents performing coding, reasoning, writing, design and data-related tasks.
overview: A library of agent skills. Each skill is a folder with a `SKILL.md` whose description tells an agent when to use it, so agents can load only what is relevant.
capabilities: Coding and design guides (code style, front-end design, agent-friendly CLIs, browser debugging over CDP).
Data skills for analysis, visualization and data storytelling.
Reasoning aids such as decision compression, blind-spot checks, red-teaming failures and evidence provenance.
Packaging for agent plugins and an installation guide.
useCases: Loading consistent working practices into coding agents.
Sharing a vetted set of agent instructions across a team.

title: Agent Skills MCP Server
summary: An MCP server that makes reusable agent skills available to compatible AI clients.
overview: A public, stateless Cloudflare Worker that exposes local `SKILL.md` files as MCP tools. A tool's description comes from the skill's front matter, and calling the tool returns the full skill.
capabilities: Each skill becomes an MCP tool, so any MCP client can discover and fetch it.
A Python build step embeds the skills into the Worker, so no skill files are needed at deploy time.
Runs locally with `npm run dev` or deploys with `npm run deploy`.
Usable as a custom connector in MCP clients; the README documents the deployed endpoint at https://anand-skill-mcp.sanand.workers.dev/mcp.
useCases: Giving chat or coding clients on-demand access to a personal skills library.
A starting point for publishing a read-only set of instructions over MCP.
note: The server has no authentication, as the README states, so it should only carry skills that are safe to publish.

title: ChatGPT to Markdown Converter
summary: A utility for converting exported ChatGPT conversation JSON into readable Markdown documents.
overview: A command-line tool that turns a ChatGPT data export (the archive folder or a `conversations.json` file) into one Markdown file per chat. The README says it also converts Claude chat exports.
capabilities: Runs with `npx chatgpt-to-markdown <archive>` with nothing to install.
Each Markdown file has YAML front matter (title, date, source) and clear User and ChatGPT headings.
Follows the active conversation branch, links exported assets and citations, and keeps reasoning or tool activity in collapsible blocks.
Handles duplicate chat titles and invalid filename characters.
useCases: Archiving chat history as searchable Markdown.
Feeding past conversations into a notes system or knowledge base.

title: Developer Productivity Scripts
summary: A collection of system configuration instructions, dotfiles and automation scripts for Windows and Linux environments.
overview: The public half of a personal setup: instructions for configuring Windows (Cygwin) and Linux laptops, shell and git configuration, and a large set of small productivity scripts.
capabilities: Setup guides for Linux, Windows and Android, plus a note on online tools that replace installed software.
Shell configuration (fish and bash), git and tmux config files.
Scripts for tasks such as backing up ChatGPT, Google and Twitter data.
A Just-driven test suite with a recipe per test module.
useCases: Rebuilding a working environment on a new machine.
Reference for dotfiles and small automation scripts.
